title: Describing Things: Common Adjectives
summary: Learn how to use common adjectives to describe people and things. Discover the correct place to put them in a sentence.

sections.p: An adjective is a word that describes a noun. A noun is a person, place, or thing. Adjectives give us more information. For example, they tell us about size, color, or how something feels. Words like big, red, and happy are all adjectives.

ex.mean: The color of the car is red.

sections.p: In English, adjectives usually go before the noun. You say the color or size first, and then the thing. For example, we say 'a big dog', not 'a dog big'. This is a very important rule to remember when you speak English.

ex.mean: My cat is small in size.
The color of his shirt is blue.

sections.p: You can also put adjectives after the verb 'to be' (am, is, are). When you do this, the adjective describes the subject at the start of the sentence. This is great for talking about how things look, feel, or are right now.

ex.mean: The temperature of the food is high.

tip: Draw pictures of objects and write their color and size next to them. Connecting words to real pictures helps your brain remember them faster!

quiz.en: I have a ___ car. It is blue.

choices: At the end of the sentence

quiz.en: She is a ___ student. She smiles a lot.
